instruction: Review each applicable case independently as a complete supplied excerpt under your current role and rubric. Assume its mathematics. Do not import context from another case or infer missing introductory prose. Identify concrete reader obstacles, not merely a preference for more explanation. Line numbers are one-based indices of the lines array.

cases.audience: Graduate readers in discrete mathematics and algorithms
lines: We study lossless fixed-length binary encodings: decoding must recover the input exactly, and shorter codewords use less storage. Fix n>=3 and let W consist of the length-n binary words with exactly one nonzero coordinate. An invertibility argument and a storage count provide the needed certificates.

Lemma 1. W can be encoded in ceil(log_2 n) bits. Proof. Encode the position of the nonzero coordinate using the binary representation of its index minus one, padded to that length. The index uniquely recovers the word.

Lemma 2. An injective map on W obtained by retaining a fixed subset of input coordinates must retain at least n-1 coordinates. Proof. If two coordinates are omitted, words supported on those coordinates both map to zero. Retaining n-1 coordinates is injective: the zero image identifies the sole omitted position.

These facts show a limitation of coordinate retention as a compression method. The second lemma gives its best possible storage, while the first supplies an alternative encoding with logarithmic storage. Thus allowing recoding can sharply improve on retaining input coordinates.

lines: Does storing a fixed subset of the original coordinates compress as well as arbitrary lossless recoding? We compare the numbers of stored bits for words in W, the length-n binary words with exactly one nonzero coordinate, where n>=3. Codewords have fixed length and must recover the input exactly.

Lemma 1. W can be encoded in ceil(log_2 n) bits. Proof. Encode the position of the nonzero coordinate using the binary representation of its index minus one, padded to that length. The index uniquely recovers the word.

Lemma 2. An injective map on W obtained by retaining a fixed subset of input coordinates must retain at least n-1 coordinates. Proof. If two coordinates are omitted, words supported on those coordinates both map to zero. Retaining n-1 coordinates is injective: the zero image identifies the sole omitted position.
The comparison is ceil(log_2 n) versus n-1 stored bits. For large n, coordinate retention can therefore be much more expensive.

cases.audience: Graduate readers familiar with Euclidean norms and linear maps
lines: For a real matrix A, let ||A|| be its operator norm induced by Euclidean length. We show that composition satisfies ||AB||<=||A||||B||, for compatible real matrices A and B.
Proof. For each unit vector x, ||ABx||<=||A||||Bx||<=||A||||B||. Taking the supremum over unit vectors x proves the claim.
